originalTitle: South Africa's president wins bid to temporarily halt impeachment inquiry over 'Farmgate'
title: President Cyril and the Farm Money Mystery!
content:
Hello, my amazing young friends all across our wonderful continent of Africa! Your friendly news reporter is here to share an important and interesting story from one of our big neighbours, South Africa. Today, we're going to talk about their special leader, President Cyril Ramaphosa. Grown-up news can sometimes sound a bit tricky, with lots of big words, but don't you worry! We'll make sure this story is super easy and fun to understand, just for you! Let's dive in!

A Surprising Story from the President's Farm

Our adventure begins a few years ago, back in 2020. President Cyril Ramaphosa, like many people, has his very own farm. It's a special place, not like a government office, but a quiet area where he keeps lovely animals. Imagine a big, green space filled with beautiful cattle – those strong, majestic cows that help on farms and give us milk. One day, something very surprising and not-so-nice happened there. Some sneaky people, like robbers, broke into his farm when no one was looking. And guess what they stole? Money! A lot of money. We're talking about cash, like the paper notes and shiny coins that your parents might use to buy yummy treats or groceries. This big theft happened quietly a while ago, but people only heard about it much, much later, which made them curious. *Did you know?* South Africa is a truly amazing country at the very bottom tip of Africa! It’s famous for its beautiful landscapes, from big mountains to sandy beaches, and for its diverse wildlife, including lions, elephants, and rhinos!

Why the Stolen Money Became a Big Question

Now, imagine you had a special secret treasure box, and someone took money from it. You'd be upset, right? But for the President's farm, it was even bigger. When everyone in South Africa finally found out about the stolen money, many people started to ask big, big questions. They wondered: "Why was there so much actual cash, like huge piles of notes, at the President's private farm? Where did all that money come from in the first place? And why didn't President Cyril tell everyone about this big problem right away when it happened, back in 2020?" These were very, very important questions because a President is like the main leader of a family – a whole country family! And leaders are supposed to be very open, honest, and tell the truth to all the people they lead. It's just like when your teacher asks you about something, and you need to tell them everything honestly. *Did you know?* A President is like the super-captain of a very big ship – that ship is their country! They work hard to make good rules and make sure everyone in the country is safe and has opportunities to learn and grow.

People Wanted to Investigate the Matter

Because of all these important questions and because the President is such an important person, some wise grown-ups in South Africa said, "We need to look into this very, very carefully!" They decided they wanted to start a special investigation. Think of it like a super-duper detective game, but for very serious grown-up things that affect the whole country. They wanted to ask President Cyril many, many questions. They wanted to check if he had followed all the important rules of the country and if everything about the money was done correctly and fairly. This special process of asking many questions and checking things is sometimes called an "inquiry." And some people even wondered if he should continue to be President if he didn't explain things perfectly. That's a huge and serious decision for a country to make! *Did you know?* Farms are incredibly important places! They grow so much of the food we eat every day, like juicy fruits, crunchy vegetables, and grains that make our bread and pap. They also keep animals that give us milk, eggs, and meat.

The President Asks for a Little Pause

But President Cyril had his own thoughts about all this. He said, "Hold on a minute! I want to make sure I tell my side of the story in the very best and clearest way possible. I believe I have good explanations for everything that happened. And I also want to make sure that the people who are asking me all these questions are doing it in a fair way, following all the correct and proper steps that our country's rules say." So, President Cyril asked a very special group of grown-ups to help him. This group works in a place called a court. A court is a serious place where very smart judges listen to problems, hear from different people, and help everyone decide what is fair and right according to the law. He asked the court if he could "pause" the big questioning time for a little bit, just to make sure everything was fair. *Did you know?* In South Africa, their money is called the Rand! It’s just like how some countries have Dollars, or Euros, or Shillings – South Africa has its own special money called Rands.

The Judges Say "Yes, You Can Pause"

And guess what happened next? The very smart and wise judges at the court listened extremely carefully to President Cyril's request. They thought about it a lot, reading many papers and thinking about all the rules. And then, they decided that it was okay for President Cyril to wait for a little while! They said, "Yes, President Cyril, you can temporarily halt this inquiry." The words "temporarily halt" mean to stop something for a little while, but not forever. It's like pressing the "pause" button on your favourite cartoon or video game when you need to go for a snack or take a quick break. The cartoon doesn't finish; it just waits for you to come back! So, the big questioning time for President Cyril is now on "pause." *Did you know?* Judges usually wear special long, black robes in court. This special clothing helps everyone know that they are important and fair people whose job it is to make big, important decisions based on the law.

What Happens Next in Our Important Story?

So, what does all this mean for our exciting story? It means that for now, President Cyril doesn't have to answer all those many, many big questions about the money found at his farm. The super-duper detective game, where grown-ups ask tough questions, is now on hold. The judges will spend more time looking at all the details and making sure everything is fair and correct. Then, later on, they will decide the next steps. It's like waiting for the next amazing episode of your favourite TV show! Eventually, the questions will be asked, and the President will explain everything, but it won't happen right now. Everyone in South Africa wants to make sure that whatever happens, it's fair, just, and done in the right way for their wonderful country and all its people. *Did you know?* Being a leader, especially a President, is a very, very big and important job! They have to make many tough decisions every day and work incredibly hard to help all the people in their country live better, happier, and safer lives.

Why This Story Matters to All of Us

This story, even though it's about grown-ups and big decisions, is important for all of us, even young friends like you across Africa. It teaches us that even presidents, who are very powerful and important, have to follow rules and explain themselves if there are questions about what they have done. It also shows us that there are special places, like courts, with wise judges, whose job it is to make sure everything is fair and that rules are followed by everyone, no matter how important they are. We all want our leaders to be honest, open, and clear with us. When they are, we can trust them more. And trust is a very, very important thing between leaders and all the people they are chosen to lead. So, keeping an eye on stories like this helps us all learn about how our countries work and why it's important to have good rules! *Did you know?* Africa is home to 54 different countries, each with its own special leader, wonderful people, and unique stories! We are all part of one big, amazing African family!

Until Next Time, My Curious Friends!

Well, that's our big news story for today, my little news explorers! It was a big story about a president, his farm, some money that was stolen, and the importance of asking questions and making sure things are fair. Remember, it's always good to be curious, ask questions, and try to understand what's happening around us in our communities and our continent. Your friendly African news reporter will be back soon with more simple, exciting, and important stories just for you. Stay curious and keep learning! Bye for now!
summary: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa won a temporary pause from big questions about money stolen from his private farm, as courts decide the fairest way to investigate.
whyMatters: This story is important because it teaches us that even powerful leaders like the President must follow rules and be honest with their country, and that special courts help make sure everything is fair for everyone.

originalTitle: Teen jailed for exam cheating in Guinea dies after sickle cell complications, father says
title: A Sad Story About Our Friend Mamadou
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends! It’s your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you important stories from our big, beautiful continent of Africa. Today, I have a story that might make your heart feel a little bit sad, but it also teaches us important lessons about being honest, trying our best, and being kind to everyone, especially those who are not feeling well. This story comes from a country called Guinea, which is a lovely place in West Africa, with friendly people and beautiful nature. It's about a young man named Mamadou. He was 17 years old. That’s much older than you, but still a young person with dreams and friends, just like you.

What Happened at School?

Mamadou was in school, just like many of you. He was taking very important tests called exams. Exams are like big quizzes that help your teachers understand how much you’ve learned and how smart you are getting! Sometimes, when people take exams, they might feel a little bit scared or worried. They might want to get the best marks. But it’s super important to always try your best and use only what *you* know. Sadly, Mamadou made a mistake during his exam. He tried to look at answers he shouldn’t have. This is called cheating. Cheating is like peeking at someone else's paper or using secret notes when you're not supposed to. It means you are not being honest about what you know. Why is cheating not good? Because it doesn't show your real learning. Learning is about working hard, asking questions, and being proud of what *you* can do all by yourself! Did you know? In many schools, if you cheat on a test, you might have to take the test again, or even get a zero mark for that test. It's much better to try your best and be honest!

Going to a Special Place

Because Mamadou made this mistake of cheating on a very important test, something serious happened. The rules for big mistakes are very strict. He was sent to a special place. This place is for people who make big mistakes that break the rules. It’s called a prison or a jail. It’s a place where people stay for a while to think about their choices and to understand why following rules is so important for everyone to live together safely and fairly. Mamadou's dad told everyone about this sad news. It’s important to remember that everyone makes mistakes sometimes, but some mistakes have bigger problems that come after them. Did you know? Rules are very important! They help us stay safe and fair with each other, whether we are at school, at home, or playing outside. Imagine playing a game without any rules – it would be very messy!

Mamadou Was Already Sick

Now, here is something very, very important to know about Mamadou. Even before he went to that special place, Mamadou had a special kind of sickness. It’s called “sickle cell.” “Sickle cell” means that some of the tiny little blood cells inside his body are not shaped perfectly round, like happy, bouncy balls. Imagine your blood cells are like tiny, round balloons carrying good food and air all around your body to keep you strong. For someone with sickle cell, some of these tiny balloons are shaped more like a crescent moon or a curved banana. These sickle-shaped cells can get stuck in tiny pipes inside the body. When they get stuck, they can stop the good food and air from getting to where they need to go. This can make people feel very tired and sometimes have a lot of pain in their bones and tummy. They need special doctors and special medicines all the time to help them feel better and stay strong. Did you know? Sickle cell is more common in parts of Africa, like Guinea, and other places where malaria used to be very common. People who have sickle cell need lots of love, care, and their special medicine every day!

Getting Very, Very Unwell

While Mamadou was in that special place, away from his home and his usual doctors, he started to get very, very sick because of his sickle cell. His body was hurting, and he needed a lot of help and his special medicine. People with sickle cell need to be very careful, especially if they are in a new or stressful place. They need their medicine, their special food, and their doctors nearby to check on them often. It sounds like Mamadou didn't get all the special care and medicine he needed to fight his sickness and keep his body strong. Mamadou’s dad said that Mamadou got sicker and sicker. It was very difficult for him. When you are sick, you need people to look after you and help you get better, right? It's even more important for someone with a special sickness like sickle cell.

Very Sad News

Sadly, because Mamadou was so very sick with his sickle cell, and he was in a place where it was very hard to get the special care he needed all the time, he became too unwell. His body couldn't fight the sickness anymore. He didn't get better. Mamadou’s dad is very, very sad, and so are his family and friends. It’s a very sad story for them. This reminds us all how important it is for everyone, especially those who are sick or have special needs, to get help, kindness, and good care. We all need to look out for each other. Did you know? When someone is very sick, doctors and nurses work super hard to make them feel better and strong again! It takes a lot of special training and a big heart to be a good doctor or nurse.

What Can We Learn?

This sad story teaches us a few important things, my friends. Let’s think about them together: First, it’s always best to be honest and try your very, very best in school. Cheating might seem like an easy way to get good marks, but it can lead to big problems and can make people sad. Being honest makes you feel strong and proud inside. Second, we must always remember to be kind and helpful to people who are sick, especially those with special conditions like sickle cell. They need extra love, understanding, and special care to stay healthy and happy. Let’s always be good friends to everyone. Third, rules are important, but we also need to make sure everyone gets the help they need if they are unwell, no matter where they are. Being kind and caring is just as important as following rules. Let’s promise to always try our best, be honest with ourselves and others, and be kind to everyone, especially our friends who might be sick or having a hard time. Helping others makes our own hearts feel happy and strong! Let’s keep Mamadou and his family in our thoughts. It’s important to learn from what happens around us so we can all make the world a better, kinder, and fairer place for everyone. That's all for today from your news reporter. Stay kind, stay curious, and always try your best!
summary: A young boy named Mamadou from Guinea got very sick and sadly did not get better after being sent to a special place for cheating on an exam, because he also had a special sickness called sickle cell.
whyMatters: This story helps us remember to always be honest and try our best in school, and it teaches us how very important it is to be kind and helpful to people who are sick, making sure they get the care they need.
